title: SRE Capacity Reconciliation and SLO Backfill Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook documents a standardized, minimally disruptive process for reconciling capacity with retrospective SLO backfills and for capturing post-incident capacity changes. It is intended for SREs owning inference-facing services (runtime, routing, caching) and their cross-functional partners (infra, product, customer success).

Goals
- Ensure SLO measurements and error-budget accounting accurately reflect changes during unobserved windows (maintenance, telemetry gaps, region migrations).
- Provide a repeatable reconciliation procedure to safely backfill SLOs without masking production regressions.
- Define post-incident capacity actions to restore safety margins and prevent recurrence.
- Integrate with incident review standards so that capacity changes are traceable and auditable.

When to use this playbook
- Telemetry gaps longer than 5 minutes occurred during a service-critical window.
- Delayed deployments or rollbacks that were not instrumented for SLO windows.
- Post-incident when capacity was pro-actively reduced/increased to mitigate an event.
- Scheduled migrations or region failovers where historical traffic split changed.

Owners and roles
- Primary owner: On-call SRE for the affected service (team rotation).
- Secondary owner: Capacity planning lead for the inference fleet.
- Reviewer: Product engineer for the dependent route(s).
- Approver (for retrospective SLO adjustments): SRE manager + Observability steward.

Key definitions
- SLO window: Measurement interval for the SLO (e.g., 30d availability; 7d p99 latency).
- Backfill: Retrospective insertion or correction of telemetry events into SLO calculations for a bounded time range.
- Reconciliation: Capacity alignment exercise ensuring available capacity matches expected load profiles after changes.

Preconditions and guardrails
- Backfills are limited to a single contiguous window no longer than 72 hours unless approved by SRE manager.
- All backfills must be recorded in the incident or change ticket with rationale, time range, and owner.
- Never backfill to improve SLOs; only to correct missing/invalid telemetry.
- If there is uncertainty about telemetry validity, create an incident and follow the incident review standard first.

Required signals and dashboards
1) SLO dashboard for the service with:
   - Error budget burn rate (1h, 6h, 24h)
   - Request rate and healthy capacity ratio
   - Regional split and cross-region latency heatmap
2) Capacity metrics:
   - GPU pool utilization (per-instance, per-queue)
   - Queue latency and queue depth per model-route
   - Autoscaler actions and recent scaling events
3) Telemetry health:
   - Trace ingestion rate and span latency
   - Metric ingestion sampling rate and agent heartbeats

Quick reference table: thresholds used in these procedures
| Signal | Warning threshold | Action threshold | Notes |
|--------|------------------:|-----------------:|-------|
| Error budget burn rate (1h) | > 2x | > 5x | Trigger review and possible capacity scaling |
| Queue depth (per-route) | > 50 reqs | > 200 reqs | Consider temporary routing/ shedding |
| Metric ingestion loss | > 1% messages | > 5% messages | Start telemetry recovery runbook |
| Pool utilization (GPU) | > 70% | > 92% | Preemptively scale or open burst capacity |

Step-by-step: SLO backfill request and approval
1) Initiate a ticket (JIRA) including:
   - A concise summary ("Backfill request: model-runtime telemetry gap 2026-02-10 03:12-03:45 UTC").
   - Start and end timestamps for the proposed backfill window.
   - Root cause: e.g., metric ingest agent restart, control plane outage, or deliberate migration.
   - Evidence: raw logs, agent-heartbeat graphs, storage-level ingestion lag.
   - Proposed correction: insert synthetic healthy events / mark range as unknown / replay events.
2) Triage (on-call SRE + capacity lead):
   - Confirm telemetry gap and verify that production behavior during the gap can be reconstructed.
   - Run a dry-run SLO calculation locally (see "Dry-run SLO backfill" below).
   - If dry-run would materially change unit SLO alerts or customer-facing SLAs, escalate to SRE manager.
3) Approve / reject:
   - Approve: SRE manager + Observability steward sign off in the ticket.
   - Reject: preserve original telemetry; add mitigation actions (e.g., improved agent monitoring).
4) Execute: follow the Execution steps below.
5) Post-execution: update SLO metadata, create an audit entry (see Audit checks).

Dry-run SLO backfill (safe validation)
- Purpose: compute the impact of the proposed backfill without modifying production SLO history.
- Steps:
  1) Export production metrics for the affected window.
  2) Apply proposed correction algorithm in a sandbox calculator (we provide a Python utility: tools/slo_tools/backfill_simulate.py).
  3) Compare resulting SLOs to baseline and record delta.
  4) If delta triggers alerting thresholds (see table above), escalate.

Execution: performing the backfill
1) Prepare: ensure the ticket contains the signed approval and the incident/change ID.
2) Lock SLO writes: write lock the SLO datastore for the target SLOs for a 15-minute window to prevent concurrent writes.
3) Run the approved backfill utility in production mode (CLI example):
   - slo-backfill --service inference-runtime --start 2026-02-10T03:12:00Z --end 2026-02-10T03:45:00Z --method replay --ticket IR-10245 --dry-run false
4) Monitor: watch the SLO dashboard and metric ingestion for 30 minutes post-run.
5) Unlock: remove write lock and confirm the computed SLO matches dry-run expectation within tolerance (±0.02 absolute).

Execution safeguards and rollback
- Safe mode: the backfill utility has a --dry-run-only flag which aborts if any of the following occur: delta > 0.05 absolute, or unusual request rate variance > 3x baseline.
- Rollback: to revert a backfill, run:
   slo-backfill --undo --ticket IR-10245 --service inference-runtime
- Audit: every backfill and undo must create an immutable audit record in the compliance log with: ticket id, operator, timestamps, and checksums of modified SLO snapshots.

Capacity reconciliation (post-change) procedure
1) Triggering events: large-scale rollouts, regional failovers, incident-driven scaling changes, or sustained error-budget erosion.
2) Data collection (single command):
   fleet-reconcile --service inference-runtime --window 72h --output /tmp/reconcile-20260215.json
   The command gathers: per-pool utilization, per-route p95 latency, autoscaler actions, admission control logs.
3) Compute residual capacity: compare expected capacity from capacity model (cap_model_v2) vs observed available capacity.
4) Actions based on residual capacity:
   - Residual > +15%: record surplus in capacity ledger and mark for potential instance drain to reduce cost.
   - Residual between -15% and +15%: annotate change and schedule re-evaluation in 48 hours.
   - Residual < -15%: immediate mitigation required (see mitigation runbook).

Mitigation runbook (if residual < -15%)
1) Short-term: toggle burst pools to ON and increase concurrency caps on non-critical routes.
2) Mid-term (1–6 hours): scale up Dedicated pools (per capacity policy) and apply traffic-shaping rules for heavy routes.
3) Long-term (>24 hours): open a capacity procurement ticket with finance if recurring shortage is forecasted.

Post-incident capacity actions and documentation
- Every incident that involved manual capacity changes must produce a "capacity action" section in the post-incident report including: what changed, why, who authorized, and whether changes were rolled back.
- Example entry: "2026-02-10 04:05 UTC — Increased pool inference-dedicated-2 by 8 cards (gpu-p4d). Authorized by SRE on-call (Maya Chen). Reason: p99 spike and queue depth. Reverted 2026-02-11 02:10 UTC after stabilization."

Integration with incident review standards
- Include capacity reconciliation artifacts (reconcile JSON, backfill dry-run deltas, audit checksums) as attachments to the incident review page.
- Use the standard post-incident classification tags: root_cause, contributing_factors, capacity_actions, monitoring_gaps.

Operational tooling and automation suggestions
- Provide a canned dashboard template: "SRE / Reconciliation / <service>" that automatically populates the signals in section "Required signals and dashboards".
- Automate dry-run calculations nightly for recent infra changes and surface anomalies to the on-call SRE Slack channel.
- Create a single CLI wrapper that performs end-to-end reconciliation and outputs a PR-compatible report for approval.

Audit checks before closing a backfill/change ticket
1) Signed approval exists in ticket.
2) Dry-run delta attached and < 0.05 absolute.
3) Audit record present in compliance log with checksum.
4) Post-run SLOs verified and annotated in SLO metadata.

Testing and drill guidance
- Run annual drills that simulate a telemetry ingestion outage and require a backfill. Assess time to approval and dry-run completion.
- Include capacity-reconciliation exercises in quarterly capacity-planning game days.

Appendices
A. Example backfill CLI usage
```
# Dry-run
slo-backfill --service inference-runtime --start 2026-02-10T03:12:00Z --end 2026-02-10T03:45:00Z --method replay --dry-run

# Execute
slo-backfill --service inference-runtime --start 2026-02-10T03:12:00Z --end 2026-02-10T03:45:00Z --method replay --ticket IR-10245
```

B. Minimal JIRA template fields
- Summary
- Start timestamp / End timestamp
- Evidence links (dashboard, logs, traces)
- Proposed correction method (replay / mark-unknown / synthetic)
- Approvers (SRE manager, Observability steward)

C. Contact matrix
- On-call SRE: oncall-inference@sre.redwood.ai
- Capacity planning lead: capacity-leads@redwood.ai
- Observability steward: obs-steward@redwood.ai

D. Change history
- 2026-02-15: v1.0 published — initial playbook and automation hooks.

If you are executing this playbook and observe any ambiguity, stop and escalate to the SRE manager.
